messages:
oliver: Quick sync — I ran an apples-to-apples KV cache benchmark to root-cause the p99 regression after the kernel-selector change. Posting notes + exact harness commands. TL;DR: regression reproduces on replay traces unless we normalize tokenization and seq-length padding; synth traffic missed it initially.

maria: can you paste the exact command + flags you used? want to reproduce locally.

oliver: yep — harness command (used in CI job `kvcache-parity`):

```bash
./tools/replay/run.py \\  --model gptx-small \\  --replay traces/2026-03-10.full.trace \\  --batch-policy '{"max_batch_size":8,"max_wait_ms":8}' \\  --kernel-modes baseline,auto,experimental \\  --kv-backend memory \\  --prefetch true \\  --warmup-steps 800 \\  --tokenizer-override tracenorm
```

oliver: important bits: `--tokenizer-override tracenorm` normalizes whitespace/token split to match on-device tokenization, and `warmup-steps` ensures prefix cache warmup before measurements.

ash: what's the difference between "replay" and your synth runs?

oliver: synth run used the same seq length distribution but we generated tokens with the runtime tokenizer (not tracenorm). that led to different prefix boundaries and fewer identical KV keys, so hit-rate was higher in synth. replay preserves the original user tokenization -> more collisions/evictions in practice.

ash: ah, so hit-rate parity requires tokenizer parity too. good call.

ash: did you try toggling kernel modes to see if selector is causing the p99?

oliver: yes — results from a 30m run (after warmup):
- baseline (old selector): replay p99=78ms, synth p99=60ms
- auto (new selector): replay p99=112ms, synth p99=64ms
- experimental-kernel: replay p99=95ms, synth p99=62ms

oliver: note the gap only shows up on replay. throughput (qps) stayed within ±3% across runs.

maria: what about KV hit-rate numbers and eviction churn?

oliver: hit-rate (measured after warmup window):
- replay: baseline=72%, auto=59%, experimental=66%
- synth: baseline=78%, auto=76%, experimental=77%

oliver: eviction churn (evicts/sec): replay auto ~420, baseline ~210. synth evicts/sec ~150 across modes.

ash: big difference. so kernel selector seems to change access patterns (maybe different kernel batch shapes reorder requests) which increases eviction pressure.

sanjay: did you capture KV correctness under concurrency? any rare mismatches?

oliver: ran concurrency correctness harness (1000 parallel clients, request skew to long prefixes). saw 0 correctness failures, but I observed increased latency tail due to thrashing. logs: `kv_cache: miss->evict_count spike at t=00:12:34, eviction_workers=4`

oliver: attached snippet from CI perf-bot: `perf-bot: https://perf.internal/runs/1813456789/results`

perf-bot: Automated report uploaded — summary + raw traces at link above. (job: kvcache-parity-2026-03-15) :rocket:

maria: action items?

oliver: shortlist:
1) reproduce locally with `--tokenizer-override tracenorm` + identical batch policy (everyone)
2) add a kernel-selector regression test that runs a small replay trace and asserts p95/p99 within delta (say +20ms)
3) instrument kernel selection path to emit `kernel.shape` tags so we can correlate shape changes to eviction spikes
4) run a focused experiment with `eviction_workers=2` vs 4 to see sensitivity

maria: I'll pick up (2) and (3). ash can you take (4)?

ash: yes, will run eviction_workers sweep and post results tomorrow.

sanjay: I'll try to craft a minimal synthetic trace that reproduces replay hit-patterns so CI runs faster.

oliver: perfect. I'll update the `kvcache-parity` job to require tokenizer-override flag and drop a short run that fails the baseline delta. thanks all. :thumbsup:
